docs.summary: Provides methods to create project assets (folders, shaders, assembly definitions, prefabs, and arbitrary typed assets) with automatic unique naming and folder index invalidation.

members.name: BeginCreateAsset
members.signature: public static void BeginCreateAsset(AssetMenuEntry entry, string relativeFolder)

docs.summary: Starts naming and creating an asset of a `[CreateAssetMenu]` type in a folder.

members.name: CreateAsset
members.signature: public static string? CreateAsset(AssetMenuEntry entry, string relativeFolder)

docs.summary: Creates an asset file from an AssetMenuEntry by instantiating its type, serializing it, and writing to disk. Returns the relative path of the created asset, or null if the folder does not exist or creation fails.
The folder new assets go into: the selected folder if there is one, otherwise the folder the project panel is currently browsing.
Converts a project-relative folder path to an absolute file-system path by combining it with the project's AssetsPath. Returns an empty string if no project is open.

members.name: FindUniqueName
members.signature: public static string FindUniqueName(string folder, string baseName, string ext)

docs.summary: Returns a unique file name in the given folder by appending a number suffix if the base name already exists.

Creates a new folder in the project at the given relative path, with a unique name and a DefaultImporter meta file. Returns the relative path of the created folder, or null if the parent folder does not exist.
Creates a new assembly definition file in the project at the given relative path, with a unique name. Returns the relative path of the created file, or null if the parent folder does not exist.

Creates a new .shader file in the project at the given relative path, with a unique name and a lit surface shader to start from. Returns the relative path of the created file, or null if the parent folder does not exist.
Creates a new .compute file in the project at the given relative path, with one kernel to start from. Returns the relative path of the created file, or null if the parent folder does not exist.
